newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber slow, except for light covering.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber slow, except for light covering.

text.p: Buyers picked up RSS3 grade rubber in modest shortcovering at the close on Thursday in the Singapore rubber market while the strong yen prompted other people to back away from the trade, dealers said.
Traders said major consumers were sniffing around for prices, but most were not in and prefered to stay on the sidelines.
"They're checking prices, but with the strong yen, most feel it will be better to stay out for the meantime," a dealer said.
"We saw better shortcovering yesterday, but everything has died down today," another dealer said.
In the meantime, foreign brokerage houses were said to be involved in a bout of modest buying for RSSE3 grade rubber, dealers said.
"The tonnages were not really that heavy. People were trying to pick up material at what they feel are bargain prices," a dealer said.
Traders said the market will be looking for further leads ahead of the weekend and will be closely looking at the yen's performance over the next few days.
At 0945 GMT, June RSS3 was seen at 111.75 U.S. cents a kg from 110.75 cents. - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
